name: floating-panel-wears-the-space-tint
description:
The floating panel must wear the space theme and follow the glass setting the way the docked sidebar does. Both now come from one native painter: the docked root paints backdrop_tint_ at backdrop_glass_alpha_ and the theme picture over it, and AtriumSidebarOverlayWidget paints that same stack under the page while the panel floats. sidebar.css paints no wash of its own any more, so the panel can never drift from the docked pane's colour.

WHY sunsetOrange AND A WHITE PAGE. The space carries sunsetOrange (#5A2E0D, triplet 90 46 13): R well above G above B, which region_mean's channel bounds can actually fail on, unlike a dark blue where only the absent min_b would separate it from grey. The page under the panel is flat white so nothing but the wash can make the region warm. chromePageTint is off in the settings fixture on purpose: left on, the core drifts the chrome toward the page's colour and a white page would wash the tint out.

The settings phase then moves the glass slider through the real settings window and reads the alpha the window pushed to the sidebar document, which is the value the native painter folds into backdrop_tint_.

assertions.label: the-page-under-the-panel-is-white
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: with the panel away this region is the flat white page, measured 255/255/255 var 0. A region that reads dark here is chrome, not page, and every measurement below would be of the wrong rectangle.

assertions.label: the-panel-is-warm-not-grey
assertions.desc: MEASURED 2026-09-07: 149.5/125.4/108.2, mean 127.7. R sits 41 above B, which is the tint and nothing else - the page under it is flat white. The old literal grey over the same page computes near 219/221/225 and fails min_r's companion bounds max_g and max_b; a panel that failed to paint reads the page's own 255 and fails them too.

assertions.label: both-glass-edits-reached-disk
assertions.desc: rules out a silent no-op on the second edit, whose own wait_vlog would have re-matched the first

assertions.label: the-frost-was-told-to-go-dark
assertions.desc: the frost's NSVisualEffectView appearance is not readable from any document, so this is its proxy: PushSidebarFrostAppearance is handed the same InkForBackdrop answer this line reports. At the staged .55 sunsetOrange composites light and the line reads black, so a white-ink line can only come from the .95 slider edit - and never from the CSS sweep, which does not reach C++.
Cmd+Q still quits cleanly after a reveal, a sweep and two settings edits
